quotes.text: The best projects start with listening, not with a design.
We wanted a site our editors enjoy using. That changed everything.
Small improvements, made every week, add up faster than one big launch.

sections.heading: Where it started
sections.body:
It began with a simple question: what do our visitors need most, and how quickly can they find it? We looked at search terms, talked to the people who use the site every day and wrote down every answer.

Those conversations shaped every decision that followed, from the structure of the pages to the words in the menu.

sections.heading: What we changed
sections.body:
We made small, careful changes instead of one big switch. Every step was tested with real content before it went live, so nothing surprised the editors on the day itself.

  • Shorter pages with clearer headings
  • Images that load at the right size
  • Content that reads well on every screen

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body:
Editors build each page from rows of content: a text, an image, a quote or a form, side by side or one below the other. The site takes care of the layout on every screen size.

That leaves more time for what matters most: what you want to say, and to whom.

sections.heading: The result
sections.body:
The new setup is easier to maintain and faster for visitors. Pages load in under a second, and editors spend less time on layout and more time on their message.

Visitors noticed too: they find what they came for sooner and stay longer.

sections.heading: What's next
sections.body:
The work isn't finished. Over the coming months we will keep measuring, listening and improving, and we will share what we learn along the way.

Have a question or an idea? Get in touch, we are happy to talk.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body:
Everything described here works on phones, tablets and large screens alike, and meets the accessibility guidelines we follow for every project.

Want to see it for yourself? The pages are live, and we are happy to give you a tour.

followUps:
We started small, with the pages people visit most. Each change was measured against how the old page performed, and only kept when it clearly helped.

Step by step the site became lighter and clearer. The structure that came out of it is now the base for every new page we add, so editors don't have to start from scratch.

Along the way we documented every choice, so the next team can build on it.

Behind every page is a team that writes, checks and updates the content. We sat down with them to understand how they work, where they lose time and what they would like to change.

Their answers led to clearer page types, fewer fields and better previews. Publishing a page now takes minutes instead of an afternoon.

And when something goes wrong, they know exactly where to look.

Good content needs good images. We chose photos that show real places and real people, cut them to the right size for every screen and gave each one a clear description for screen readers.

The result is a site that loads fast, looks sharp on every device and tells the same story to everyone who visits it.

Every image now has a purpose on the page it's on.

Accessibility was part of the plan from the first sketch. We checked contrast, headings and keyboard navigation on every page type, and tested with people who use a screen reader every day.

Many of the fixes were small: a clearer label, a better link text, a heading in the right order. Together they make the site easier for everyone, not only for those who need it most.

sections.heading: What to expect
sections.body:
The programme is built around meeting people and trying things out. There is room for questions throughout, and the hosts are happy to help you get started.

No experience needed: everyone is welcome, whether you come alone or with friends.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body:
The venue is accessible for wheelchairs and pushchairs. Drinks are available on site.

  • Come a few minutes early
  • Bring a water bottle
  • Children are welcome

sections.heading: Programme
sections.body:
We start with a short welcome, followed by the main part of the event. Afterwards there is time to chat and look around.

The exact times can change slightly; keep an eye on this page for updates.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
The venue is a short walk from the station and the bus stop. Bicycle parking is available at the entrance.

Coming by car? Use the public car park nearby; spaces are limited on busy days.

followUps:
Last year the event drew visitors from all over the region. This edition builds on what they told us: more space, more shade and more time to talk.

Volunteers welcome you at the entrance and show you around. Have an idea for a next edition? Let us know on the day.

The hosts have prepared everything you need. You only have to bring your curiosity and, if you like, a notebook for ideas to take home.

Places are limited, so the first come are the first served. Sold out? We keep a waiting list.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body:
Visitors decide within seconds whether a page is what they need. Clear structure and wording help them decide faster, and help search engines understand the page.

Small improvements here pay off on every page you publish.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.body:
1. Start with what the visitor wants to know or do
  2. Write it down in one plain sentence
  3. Check it on a phone, not only on your screen
  4. Ask a colleague to read it once

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Most problems come from writing for ourselves instead of for the visitor: internal names, long sentences and vague links.

  • Jargon in titles
  • "Click here" links
  • Images without a description

sections.heading: In practice
sections.body:
Take one page you know well and go through it with these tips in mind. Note what you would change, then change it.

Repeat this every few months: content gets outdated faster than you think.

followUps:
You don't have to do everything at once. Start with the pages that get the most visitors, improve them, and see what changes in your statistics.

What works there usually works on the rest of the site too, so you can apply it step by step.

Not sure where to start? Look at the questions people ask your team most often. The answers often belong on the website, written in the same words people use.

That is also how you find the right title for a page.
